# Agent states

<!-- Generated by tools/docs/states-doc.ts from packages/agent/src/state/mapping.ts. Do not edit. -->

The state machine (`packages/agent/src/state`) turns the normalised engine events and runner signals into the contract's state names (CT-STATE-MAP). It works the same for Claude Code and Codex because it never sees raw CLI output.

## Event to state

| Input | State | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `turn.started` | `prompt-received` | 600 ms, then the state below |
| `thinking.delta` | `thinking` | planning in plan mode; thinking-hard after 15 s without output |
| `text.delta` | `streaming` |  |
| `tool.requested (read)` | `reading-file` |  |
| `tool.requested (search)` | `searching` |  |
| `tool.requested (web)` | `searching` |  |
| `tool.requested (edit)` | `editing-file` |  |
| `tool.requested (create)` | `creating-file` |  |
| `tool.requested (delete)` | `deleting-file` |  |
| `tool.requested (command)` | `running-command` |  |
| `tool.requested (subagent)` | `sub-agent` |  |
| `tool.requested (background)` | `background-task` |  |
| `tool.requested (mcp)` | `tool-running` |  |
| `tool.requested (other)` | `tool-running` | also any unknown tool |
| `tool.result` | `(previous open tool, else thinking)` | tests-pass / tests-fail when the command was a test run |
| `subagent.started` | `sub-agent` |  |
| `approval.requested` | `awaiting-approval` | stays until every open approval is resolved; no other event (warning, error, compaction, tool, text, merge-conflict, saving, a dwell timer) displaces it. Only approval.resolved, turn.done, interrupt and exit leave it |
| `approval.resolved (approve)` | `approved` | 800 ms, then back to work |
| `approval.resolved (deny)` | `denied` | 800 ms, then back to work |
| `question.asked` | `asking-question` | stays until the next work event |
| `compaction.started` | `compacting` | until compaction.ended |
| `turn.done (ok)` | `success` | 2 s, then idle |
| `turn.done (error)` | `error` | 2 s, then idle |
| `turn.done (canceled)` | `idle` |  |
| `engine.warning` | `warning` | 2 s, then back to work |
| `error (provider_cap_reached / provider_rate_limited)` | `warning` | plus a local hint for the UI; the wire state stays warning |
| `error (fatal, other)` | `error` |  |
| `signal: exited crash` | `crash` | the machine then ignores everything |
| `signal: interrupt` | `idle` |  |
| `signal: merge_conflict / saving` | `merge-conflict / saving` | 2 s |
| `idle for 15 min` | `sleeping` | any turn.started wakes it |

When several tools are open at once the newest one is shown; when it closes the previous one is shown, then `thinking`. Open approvals are tracked by id: while any is open the state is `awaiting-approval` and settling always returns to it. Tool kinds come from the tool name (and, for shell tools, the first word of the command: `cat` is a read, `rg` a search, `rm` a delete).

## Timing

- `prompt-received`: 600 ms, then back to the work state or `idle`
- `approved`: 800 ms, then back to the work state or `idle`
- `denied`: 800 ms, then back to the work state or `idle`
- `success`: 2000 ms, then back to the work state or `idle`
- `error`: 2000 ms, then back to the work state or `idle`
- `warning`: 2000 ms, then back to the work state or `idle`
- `tests-pass`: 2000 ms, then back to the work state or `idle`
- `tests-fail`: 2000 ms, then back to the work state or `idle`
- `merge-conflict`: 2000 ms, then back to the work state or `idle`
- `saving`: 2000 ms, then back to the work state or `idle`
- `thinking` becomes `thinking-hard` after 15 s without engine output.
- `idle` becomes `sleeping` after 15 min; a new turn wakes it.

## What goes on the wire

Only the contract's agent-level states are sent in `agent.state`: `approved`, `asking-question`, `awaiting-approval`, `background-task`, `compacting`, `crash`, `creating-file`, `deleting-file`, `denied`, `deploying`, `editing-file`, `error`, `idle`, `merge-conflict`, `planning`, `reading-file`, `ready`, `running-command`, `saving`, `searching`, `streaming`, `sub-agent`, `success`, `tests-fail`, `tests-pass`, `thinking`, `thinking-hard`, `tool-running`, `warning`. `prompt-received` and `sleeping` are real contract state names but are not in that list, so they only go to the local UI. At most 2 frames per agent per second, never the same state twice in a row, payload `{agent_id, state, since}` only.

Client-local states (connectivity, account, provider, limits, social) are never produced here. Cap and rate-limit errors from the engine are passed to the UI as a hint while the wire state stays `warning`.
